entry.title: Halzen Nobel Prize
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The Royal Swedish Academy of Science announced on 6 October that the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics goes to Francis Halzen, principal investigator of IceCube, for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin. Wisconsin Public Radio has since interviewed him about the award and the importance of neutrino research. The whole station gathered at the IceCube Lab at the South Pole for a celebratory group photo.

entry.title: DUNE sensor production
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. UK scientists and engineers have completed half of the 137 Anode Plane Assemblies that the UK is producing for DUNE. These sensors will detect the tiny electrical signals produced when neutrinos interact with liquid argon in DUNE's underground detectors.

entry.title: KM3NeT infrastructure
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The KM3NeT Collaboration announced on 16 October that it has been recognised as a Landmark in the ESFRI Roadmap 2026. The ESFRI Roadmap identifies major European research infrastructures. On the construction side, Cable Termination Frame 3 was installed at the ARCA deep-sea site during a marine campaign, one of two steps reported for ARCA and ORCA.

entry.title: JUNO-TAO commissioning
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The Taishan Antineutrino Observatory is the JUNO satellite that measures the reactor antineutrino spectrum at 43.2 m from a reactor core. It uses a 2.8-ton liquid-scintillator detector read out by 4,024 silicon photomultiplier tiles. Installation was completed in 2025 and physics data taking began on 10 February 2026. The JUNO Collaboration reports stable cryogenic operation, with about 90% of the readout channels retained.

entry.title: Baikal-GVD point sources
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Baikal-GVD is under construction in Lake Baikal and is now 70% complete. A search for point-like astrophysical neutrino sources in its 2019-2024 track-like dataset found no significant source. Upper limits were computed for a selection of candidate objects and compared with published IceCube, ANTARES and KM3NeT results.

entry.title: Neutrino cross section
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. A new analysis of IceCube data determines muon-neutrino-nucleon charged-current cross sections across the TeV scale. The authors note that existing measurements still carry uncertainties of about 20-40% and that no single measurement covers the range from sub-TeV to tens of TeV.

entry.title: Fast X-ray transients
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. A time-integrated search used 14 years of public IceCube muon-track data for neutrinos from 27 fast X-ray transients detected by Einstein Probe. No statistically significant excess was found. The largest test statistic was TS=4.77 for EP240801a, with a local p-value of 0.04, and 90% confidence level upper limits on the muon-neutrino flux were derived.

entry.title: P-ONE photomultipliers
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. P-ONE is a planned cubic-kilometre-scale neutrino telescope for the Pacific Ocean, using infrastructure operated by Ocean Networks Canada. Its first detector line will carry 320 3-inch Hamamatsu R14374-10 photomultiplier tubes. All of the tubes were characterised before deployment to check them against the detector acceptance criteria.

entry.title: The paper proves that, in open two-flavour neutrino oscillations, every completely positive trace-preserving e
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper proves that, in open two-flavour neutrino oscillations, every completely positive trace-preserving evolution covariant under rotations of the mass-coherence plane is exactly blind to the Majorana phase. It also identifies, for the unital Pauli-GKSL class, when a rate anisotropy can supply the phase reference needed to see it. This is relevant to anyone asking whether decoherence could ever reveal the Dirac or Majorana nature of neutrinos.

entry.title: The authors compute the two-neutrino double-beta decay rate with the full interdependence of nuclear structure
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors compute the two-neutrino double-beta decay rate with the full interdependence of nuclear structure and lepton kinematics, without the usual closure, non-closure or Taylor-expansion approximations. They present the resulting deviations in decay rates and electron spectra for 82Se and 136Xe. The spectra matter to double-beta decay searches because those searches model the two-neutrino mode as a background.

entry.title: The paper studies neutrino mass and thermal leptogenesis in the Babu-Nandi-Tavartkiladze model, which has a sc
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper studies neutrino mass and thermal leptogenesis in the Babu-Nandi-Tavartkiladze model, which has a scalar quadruplet and two vectorlike fermion triplets. Neutrino masses arise from a dimension-7 operator at tree level and a dimension-5 operator at one loop, accommodating sub-eV masses with new physics at the TeV scale. It asks whether thermal leptogenesis is viable in a framework that differs from canonical seesaw leptogenesis.

entry.title: The paper builds a gauged U(1) L_mu - L_tau extension with an ultralight vector boson that mixes kinetically w
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper builds a gauged U(1) L_mu - L_tau extension with an ultralight vector boson that mixes kinetically with the photon. This generates an extra matter potential in the Sun that modifies MSW flavour conversion. The author uses recent solar neutrino measurements from Borexino, SNO and Super-Kamiokande and discusses prospects for JUNO and XLZD.

entry.title: The paper examines whether neutrinos from past Galactic core-collapse supernovae could be detected through nuc
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper examines whether neutrinos from past Galactic core-collapse supernovae could be detected through nuclear recoil tracks in ancient minerals, known as paleodetectors. It varies the neutron-star mass, includes failed supernovae that form black holes, and considers the nuclear equation of state. Sensitivity is found to be enhanced for models with larger neutrino emission.

entry.title: The paper studies Delta-direct-Urca neutrino emission in neutron-star matter containing Delta isobars, noting
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper studies Delta-direct-Urca neutrino emission in neutron-star matter containing Delta isobars, noting that the specific contribution of this process to neutrino emissivity had not been explicitly examined. Nucleonic and hyperonic Urca processes are considered dominant cooling mechanisms. The paper matters to neutrino physicists as a case where neutrino emission controls the thermal evolution of dense matter.
